record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports pruning experiments on random base models, testing whether its training-based pruning method also works in that setting. It does not test the listed claims about training from random initialization to near-zero training classification error, bad minima in teacher-student networks, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization speed.
record.gate_note: The paper studies structured pruning of pretrained networks, with an additional experiment pruning random base models. It reports test accuracy, Jacobian singular values and retraining curves, but not training classification error for the claim versions. Results cited from other studies are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses signal propagation and dynamical isometry ideas to develop a pruning method, then evaluates pruning performance and retraining. It does not test any listed version: orthogonalization after pruning is not an initialization comparison, learning rates are not related to a stability threshold, and BN regularization is not a BN-versus-no-BN comparison. Figure 8 measures training accuracy during retraining of pretrained, pruned models, rather than training from random initialization as V1 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their filter-decorrelation and BN-parameter regularization preserve trainability during structured pruning and improve pruning performance. Equivalence to the oracle recovery method is demonstrated on linear MLPs; on nonlinear CNNs, they report favorable pruning comparisons, especially under aggressive pruning.
record.recipe_differences: The method regularizes filters and batch-normalization parameters while pruning pretrained networks, then removes filters and retrains. The random-base-model experiment applies pruning to random models; neither setup tests the claim versions' training-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported pruning performance varies with pruning ratio and retraining learning rate; hyperparameter sensitivity is examined for regularization interval and granularity.

fits_no_version.finding: On random-base ResNet56/CIFAR10, TPP exceeds L1 pruning in test accuracy at every tested pruning ratio; at PR 0.95, accuracies are 85.36% versus 82.68% (Table 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trainability-preserving regularization improves test accuracy after structured pruning of random-base networks.

fits_no_version.finding: On linear MLP/MNIST, post-pruning orthogonalization and TPP improve Jacobian singular values and early retraining test accuracy, reducing differences between the two retraining learning-rate schedules (Figure 3; Tables 11–12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving or recovering signal propagation after pruning can accelerate retraining and reduce sensitivity to retraining learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 explicitly reports faster training-accuracy improvement with TPP than L1 pruning at PR 0.9 and 0.95 for pretrained ResNet56/CIFAR10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving trainability during aggressive structured pruning accelerates subsequent optimization.

record.problems: The reported evidence centers on pruning performance and test accuracy rather than the claim versions' training-error outcomes. ImageNet results are not run multiple times because of resource limits; the authors describe them as generally stable.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the experiments measure pruning outcomes, test accuracy, and Jacobian singular values, not a behavior named by any listed version. Figure 8 shows training-accuracy curves during retraining, but the accompanying text describes optimization acceleration at high pruning ratios rather than testing the claim versions' training-from-initialization outcomes.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe effects. Random-base pruning experiments report test accuracy.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, very deep plain tanh training, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, initialization-dependent learning speed or trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to a learning-rate stability threshold, including recovery, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BN, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the reader's tests/T3 classification to uses_without_test/T4. The empty qualifying-row set is appropriate. Orthogonalization failures on nonlinear pruned CNNs do not challenge V4's initialization claims. The relevant excluded results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test training large convolutional networks from random initialization to zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, or the effects of model size and early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or spurious-local-minima result.
No comparison of plain and residual networks by depth or training error; no test of deep plain tanh networks or normalization-free residual training.
No test of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, or training plain convolutional networks at extreme depth.
No test of training with learning rates above a stability limit, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, or divergence relative to a stability threshold.
No comparison of batch normalization versus no normalization for speed or learning-rate tolerance; BN is regularized as part of pruning.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
